PASS: Gate-1 audit of c27a566 (HEAD). Sprint file re-read fresh; unchanged since 9fc57e7 (planning) apart from d82ccc9's lifecycle status line.

R1 MET: app/reading/[id]/HoroscopeReveal.tsx aspectsNoteText now returns `Revealed on request from 10 positions and ${aspectCount} aspects.` Only the first word changed; the aspectCount interpolation is untouched.
R2 MET: lib/date-page/cast.ts CAST_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE now reads "The horoscope can't be revealed right now because the service is unavailable. Try again in a few minutes." Only "written" -> "revealed".
R3 MET: diff is 3 files, 4 lines: the two string literals plus the two test expectations. No logic, markup or style change. CAST_DISABLED_MESSAGE and CAST_SAVE_FAILED_MESSAGE are unchanged. grep for "Written on request" and "can't be written" under app/ and lib/ finds nothing (grep exit 1).
R4 MET: ReadingPanel.test.ts lines 144 and 188 updated in wording only; the matcher shapes (toMatch with the aria-hidden regex, toContain) are identical, and no assertion was removed (1-for-1 line swaps). The outage message has no literal assertion anywhere: lib/date-page/cast.test.ts lines 114 and 126 assert against the imported CAST_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE constant, so they follow the change without an edit, which R4 allows.

Checks, re-run by QA1 at c27a566 with exit codes read directly, not from output tails: npm run lint exit=0; npm run typecheck exit=0; npm test exit=0 (350 passed); npm run build exit=0. I did not rely on the Dev Team handoff for this evidence.

Observation, not a defect: other user-facing "written" copy remains, e.g. "Recently written" in app/date/[date]/DateNavigation.tsx and the site description in app/layout.tsx. Both are explicitly out of scope ("Any other copy change"; R3 "no other messages change"). If the user wants them aligned, that is a future proposal for Master Controller.

No Human Prerequisites. No known-failing tests.

PASS: PASS (round 1). Tested 2026-11-23, about 13:50 UTC, against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.

commit d77911b, migrationVersion unchanged at 20261122152710. git diff --stat c27a566 d77911b touches
only docs/sprints/state/sprint-35.json.
CI: runs 45185314125 (c27a566) and 45186273300 (d77911b). Both succeeded.
Tools: headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) with JS on and off, at 1280x900 and 390x844, plus curl
against the served HTML and every served JS chunk.

STEP 1, metadata line after reveal: PASS, observed live.
I revealed the saved horoscope (a real click on the "Reveal the horoscope" summary) on 5 pages. After
the reveal, the open panel's paragraph reads, verbatim:
- /date/1969-07-20: "Revealed on request from 10 positions and 17 aspects."
- /reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d: "Revealed on request from 10 positions and 17 aspects."
- /date/2030-03-14: "Revealed on request from 10 positions and 16 aspects."
- /date/2050-06-15: "Revealed on request from 10 positions and 13 aspects."
- /date/2026-12-16: "Revealed on request from 10 positions and 11 aspects."
The aspect count N still varies per date (17, 16, 13, 11), so it is still computed and not hard-coded.
Results were identical with JS on and with JS off.
The URL was unchanged, there were zero non-prefetch requests during the reveal, and there were no
console or page errors. The /reading page made the same two Go-to-this-date _rsc prefetches seen in
Sprint 33.
The same wording also shows in the folded state on desktop, as an aria-hidden span beside the button.
Screenshot: s35-desk-folded.png.
"Written on request" appears nowhere in the served HTML of /date/1969-07-20, /date/2031-05-09 or
/reading/0b01c79f-..., nor in any of the 9 JS chunks they load: 0 hits.

Observation, not a defect and not new: at 390px the metadata line is not shown at all, folded or
revealed. Both elements carry the footerNote and desktopOnly classes and compute display none on the
phone. Sprint 35 changed only the string literal (c27a566 diff: one line each in HoroscopeReveal.tsx
and cast.ts, plus two test lines), so this is the existing desktop-only design. My Sprint 33 phone
screenshot s33-m390-saved-open.png likewise has no line under the revealed text.

STEP 2, outage message: PASS. Checked from the deployed source, NOT observed live, as the sprint file
specifies. Triggering the outage safely in production isn't possible.
- At the deployed commit d77911b, lib/date-page/cast.ts lines 10-11 read: CAST_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE =
  "The horoscope can't be revealed right now because the service is unavailable. Try again in a few
  minutes."
- It is used at lines 64 and 78.
- git grep at d77911b for "Written on request" or "can't be written" under app/ and lib/ found
  nothing (exit 1).
- The message is server-side only: neither "can't be revealed" nor "service is unavailable" appears in
  the served client JS (0 hits), so there was no client-side copy to observe.
